sections.title: Intermediate Korean II
sections.description: This is a continuation of Intermediate Korean I. This course is designed to develop students' Korean language proficiency to the intermediate-mid level of the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines. This course expands student's competence by dealing with more functions in various contexts that students can frequently encounter in everyday interactions. In order to prepare students for social contexts, students are encouraged to engage in conversations by personalizing the topics, functions or contexts. Students will perform in an interpersonal way by providing and obtaining information, expressing feelings and emotions, and exchanging opinions on a variety of topics such as birthday parties, recreation and hobbies, Korean holidays, marriage, cultural differences, education and jobs. This course completes the College language requirement.

sections.title: Intermediate Korean II (Penn Global Seminar)
sections.description: KORN0401 is the second semester of intermediate-level Korean. As a Penn Global seminar course, it aims to enhance students’ linguistic and cultural competence in Korean. Under the overarching theme of exploring Korea’s past and present, students will have ample opportunities to explore and engage in real language use and learn various cultural perspectives, practices, and products. In addition, students will collaborate on a bilingual mini research project with language partners, focusing on a topic of their choice related to various aspects of Korean culture and society (e.g., history, language, architecture, music, art, food, etc.). The travel component includes visits to cultural sites, historical monuments, museums, exhibits, and educational institutions to gain an in- depth understanding of Korea’s past and present. Upon completion of the course, students are expected to achieve the Intermediate Mid level based on the ACTFL (American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages) proficiency scale.
